contextual_sources.observation: The company history records delivery of steamships Varna, Sofia and Kiril in 1903–1906, and wartime mobilization of company vessels in 1916–1918.
contextual_sources.role: Supports the existence of a period steamer named Varna; does not establish this telegram, voyage, horse shipment or exact ship identity.

limits: The unchanged source has 225 slots under RICHI-220; the five source exclusions and all 21 previously minimizing frame maps remain conditional and unchanged.

The repeated spans and their equal-length correspondence are explicit hypotheses. Shared letters are inferred at the minimum extra observed-coordinate cost of making each pair identical, not directly observed at the missing slots.

The common layer transfers only N35, R40 and L81. It preserves the conflicting U/A and U/Y observations and the literal 4 between the first two names, so it does not itself assert identical whole names.
Exactly two minimum equal-copy variants survive for each field. All four joint variants are retained, including VURNA and BYRDAL; none is selected as historically unique.
VARNA is a plausible named-ship reading with external contextual support. No September voyage or particular hull is identified, and BURDAL/BYRDAL is not silently converted to Burgas.
The opening remains unresolved, all numeric labels and raw 4 are retained, and no additional source map or key assignment is introduced. This extension adds no physical source record.
